newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-New Australia wheat to go ahead despite fears.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-New Australia wheat to go ahead despite fears.

text.p: Australia's new longseason feed wheat industry would not be halted by a sometimes-irrational debate about stem rust, the managing director of the Australian Wheat Board, John Lawrenson, said on Thursday.

Lawrenson was commenting on a debate about the introduction of a new longseason feed wheat variety to growing areas after the discovery of limited amounts of stem rust in the new winter wheat. Many commercial varieties of wheat, both feed and milling, were not stem rust resistant, Lawrenson said.
"Any outbreak on longseason wheats in spring will happen long after the traditional wheat crop areas have been harvested," he said in a statement.
"Stem rust on feed wheats doesn't pose any risk at all to milling wheats," he said. "The suggestion that the feed wheat industry be stopped is ludicrous."
Proper management and monitoring of growing programmes could ensure that stem rust risks were very low, he said.
